title: What the film shows: autoradiography, northern blot and overexpression
summary: Cells make RNA with radioactive uridine, or with an X expression vector, and the RNA is run on a gel against film. Place the bands, then see what the film really shows. Each later round changes one thing.

spec.intro: Cells were left to make RNA for an hour. Their RNA was extracted, separated by size on a gel and laid against X-ray film. Untreated cells make about three times as much of the housekeeping RNA, H, as of X. Work out what the film shows in each lane.
spec.lesson: Radioactive uridine goes into every new RNA, so the film shows all the RNA that was made, darker where there is more, and nothing where the uridine was not radioactive.

lanes.name: Cells with an X expression vector
lanes.detail: A strong promoter keeps X switched on, at about ten times its usual level. Radiolabelled uridine.

lanes.name: Cells with an inducible X vector, no IPTG
lanes.detail: The Lac repressor is on the operator. Radiolabelled uridine.

changes.say: A northern blot instead: the film is read through a radioactive probe that matches X, added to the separated RNA and then washed off, not through the uridine label.
changes.lesson: A northern blot lights up only the RNA the probe matches, however the RNA was labelled, so lane 2 shows X too.

changes.say: The probe is swapped for one that matches the housekeeping RNA, H.
changes.lesson: Only H matches this probe, and the cells make the same amount of H in every lane, so every lane shows the same band.

changes.say: IPTG is left out of the last lane.
changes.lesson: Without IPTG the Lac repressor stays on the operator, so X is made at its usual low level.

why.say: That lane had ordinary uridine, so none of its RNA is radioactive and the film stays clear.
why.misconception: Expected RNA to show on film without a radioactive label

why.say: The probe matches X only, so H does not show, even though it is in every lane.
why.misconception: Expected every RNA to show when only one is probed

why.say: This probe does not match X, so X does not show.
why.misconception: Expected every RNA to show when only one is probed

why.say: The vector makes many times more X than the cell usually does, and a darker band means more RNA.
IPTG frees the operator, so the inducible vector makes X and the band is darker.
X is the longer RNA (2.4 kb against 1.3 kb), so it moves less far through the gel.

spec.note: Only two RNAs are drawn; a real lane holds many. Real bands carry some noise; here the same amount always gives the same darkness.
